text:
Predicates:
TakeGRE(x) ::: x takes the GRE test.
Cost(x, y) ::: It costs x US $y to take the GRE test.
ProvideFinancialAid(x, y) ::: ETS provides financial aid to y GRE applicants.
Prove(x, y) ::: x proves y.
EconomicHardship(x) ::: x experiences economic hardship.
Have(x, y) ::: x has y.
LiveIn(x, y) ::: x lives in y.
SingleParentFamily(x) ::: x is in a single-parent family.
OutOfWork(x, y) ::: x has been out of work for more than y year.
Premises:
Cost(TakeGRE, 205) ::: It costs US $205 to take the GRE test.
∀x (TakeGRE(x) → ∃y (ProvideFinancialAid(ETS, x) ∧ Prove(x, EconomicHardship(x)))) ::: ETS provides financial aid to those GRE applicants who prove economic hardship.
∀x (EconomicHardship(x) ↔ (Have(x, little money) ∨ Have(x, few resources))) ::: Economic hardship refers to difficulty caused by having too little money or too few resources.
∃x (LiveIn(Tom, SingleParentFamily) ∧ Have(Tom, dad) ∧ OutOfWork(dad, 1)) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family. His dad has been out of work for more than a year.
Conclusion:
∃y (ProvideFinancialAid(ETS, TakeGRE)) ::: Tom can apply for financial aid from ETS to take the GRE test.
